title: Review of c26's predator persistence vs arena size: at 192^2 on fresh seeds 3 and 4 the specialist predator lasts 140 and 260 t after introduction, against c26's 90-120 t; the small-arena extinction replicates, but the spread at 192^2 reaches the 224^2 value, so the 'threshold near 224^2' is not yet resolved from a smooth rise
summary: Ran c26's runle.py on the parent arena world (WORLD_P PRED 1, T_INTRO 200, PSIG 8, DECB 0.002, DOMAIN 192) on fresh seeds 3 and 4 to t=500, plus a short labkit run of the same world (seed 3, t=30). Seed 3: predators peak at 25 cells, prey fall from 40 to 5, the last predator cell is seen at t=340 (140 t after introduction), and prey recover to 47 by t=500. Seed 4: predators peak at 22, prey fall from 39 to 16, a small predator population lingers at 1-8 cells and is gone after t=460 (260 t), prey back at 40 (data/sz192_s4.png). Both runs show the predator going extinct in the small arena as c26 reports, but seed 4's 260 t equals c26's 224^2 seed-1 value (250 t), so with 2 seeds per size the persistence at 192-224^2 overlaps.

observations.finding: persistence.txt: 192^2 predator persistence 140 t (seed 3) and 260 t (seed 4) vs c26's 90 and 120 t; data/sz192_s4.png: predator cells 22 -> 1-8 -> 0 by t=470, prey recover

seeds_run.result: predator extinct 140 t after introduction (small-arena extinction replicates)
predator extinct 260 t after introduction, longer than c26's 192^2 runs and equal to its 224^2 seed 1

verdicts.limitation: Only 192^2 re-run (no 224^2 or 256^2), 2 fresh seeds, t=500; persistence is one extinction time per run and its spread is large (90-260 t across 4 runs at 192^2), so a sharp threshold needs more seeds per size. The labkit run is a 30 t visual check only.
